b: I've been job hunting for 2 years. My resume is unique and my previous industry is barely alive (blogging). I have a ton of transferrable skills but after hundreds of applications and a dozen or so interviews and two final stage interviews, keep getting rejected with "someone else who more closely matches what we're looking for."

I've gotten 3 short-term contracts (there was no potential for advancement - think small businesses needing seasonal help) and was a freelancer for 10 years so don't think I'm a bad interviewee. I've been doing a lot of odd jobs (substitute teaching, dog walker, cleaner) to stay afloat. But nobody will hire me full-time.

I feel my brain turning to mush. I graduated high school + college early (a decade ago) while working nearly full-time. I used to read a lot but can barely focus on 2 pages before I become exhausted (I still try to listen to audiobooks).

I recently made it to a final interview but unfortunately they ended up choosing a girl who had more experience in the tech world. I recently landed a small design project and am struggling to get through it. My brain is MUSH.

In general, I feel like life's also thrown a lot at me the past few years which hasn't helped. I had some health stuff and lived out of my car for a few years to avoid debt and build some savings. Figuring out my next shower, cheap meal, bathroom, etc. was exhausting but I made it work and am back in stable housing.
I genuinely don't see a future at all considering people who have crazy impressive resumes are struggling to find jobs.
